loopIdea: The closing beat settles back into the same extreme macro of the tread groove with the copper coin standing on edge under the same harsh work light, so a replay begins at the start of the same push-in.
mechanicTruth: Tread depth is what moves water out from under the tire, and a penny stood head-down in the groove measures it: if the tread still covers the top of Lincoln's head there is depth left, and if the whole head shows the groove is down around two thirty-seconds of an inch. Read the inner rib, the center and the outer rib separately, because tread rarely wears evenly across one tire.
selectedCaption: 10-second tire check anyone can do at home. If you can see the top of Lincoln's head, it's time. Swing by — we'll check all four, no charge.
voiceoverScript: A penny reads tread better than a glance. Head down, into the groove. Whole head showing means low tread. Check inner, center, outer. Shallow tread needs more road in rain.
